utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Registrar, would you please call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case IT-05-87-A, the Prosecutor versus Nikola Sainovic, Nebojsa Pavkovic, Vladimir Lazarevic, and Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. May I now please have the appearances of the parties. First, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Jonathan MacDonald and Kyle Wood on behalf of the Prosecution and our Case Manager Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And now Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. My name is Toma Fila, representing Nikola Sainovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Aleksandar Aleksic representing the Defence of Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mihajlo Bakrac, representing General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Lead counsel Branko Lukic and co-counsel Dragan Ivetic representing Mr. Sretan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we start, can all the parties hear the proceedings in a language that they understand? Yes, Mr. Sainovic. THE APPELLANT SAINOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can follow. THE APPELLANT PAVKOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can follow. THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. THE APPELLANT LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. This requires a Status Conference to be convened every 120 days during the appeal proceedings to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and the physical condition of that person. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on the 13th May, 2013. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order issued 11 July 2013. First, I would like to inquire into the status of the detention conditions and the health situation of the appellants. If you have any concerns in relation to the detention conditions, or your state of health that cannot be resolved through the standard procedures, I would invite you to raise them now. If you wish, this discussion can take place in private session. Yes, yes, Mr. Lazarevic. THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for giving me the floor today. Allow me to inform you briefly in a couple of sentences about my health; namely, my dental health and the news between these two Status Conferences to update you. Five months ago, the people in charge of my medical care rejected the request of my Defence to finally successfully resolve, after five years, the very complex problems of my dental health by putting in implants and fixed dentures. They have decided, for the seventh time in five years, to try to put in mobile dentures in my upper and lower jaw, trying to do the impossible. During our last Status Conferences and immediately prior to that, there was a glimmer of hope that there could perhaps be a more successful way of treating my dental problems. Even the president of the Tribunal, the esteemed Judge Meron showed interest in resolving my health issues, showed interest in my health condition by issuing two written decisions in mid-July. The medical services in charge of my health in the Detention Unit spent one month and a half working on this, and on the 2nd of July of this year I was given the seventh dentures for the upper jaw and for the first time for the lower jaw, which in the meantime suffered further degradation. I said way back a year ago that in five years I be reduced to just six teeth in my jaw. The new dentures given to me for my upper jaw is somewhat of an improvement in relation to the previous dentures, and I continue wearing it but only to improve my pronunciation. That is the only use I have of it. I cannot use it for its basic purpose, which is to process food. The dentures for the lower jaw I could only wear for a maximum of a couple of hours at the time, since it was given to me on the 2nd of July. This piece of dentures also cannot be used when eating. Two adjustments were made but did not yield any results; that is to say, that in the past four months, the measures taken by the medical services produced no results, no satisfactory results in treating my seriously deteriorating dental health. As to what is going to happen next, I truly don't know. What do I and my Defence need to do next is, again, a question that I have no answer to. Mr. President, in order to portray the seriousness and the dramatic state of this health issue of mine, which has been going on for a very long time, please allow me to quote the evaluation of a competent medical expert. In a medical article published recently, this person wrote about the correlation between a proper nutrition, dental health, and the so-called inflammatory disease of the abdominal tract. All of these conditions are present in my case, they are chronic and have been going on for a long time. The article I'm quoting is an article written by one of the top specialists in the south-east Europe, an expert who is an oncologist and a gastroenterologist and works at the military medical academy in Belgrade, in Serbia, Professor Dino Tarabar. This specialist is familiar with my medical issues, and we got to know each other in June of last year when he was a member of the medical team from Serbia who examined me. Now speaking about this correlation between dental health and proper nutrition as well as the inflammatory disease of the gut, says the following: That this condition cannot be treated with the current therapy that I'm receiving. So Professor Dino Tarabar, when speaking of this correlation says that: "Nutrition and food taken in orally in these kinds of conditions is extremely important. A patient has to chew all pieces of food until they become liquid and only then swallow them." This professional medical opinion is something that I fully understand. Unfortunately, I don't know who is going to assist me in ensuring that I can do that so that I reach the state of a stable remission, a state of illness which would be bearable for a detainee such as myself. Mr. President, that's all I had to say. Thank you for your attention and understanding. Thank you, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I take note of your submissions. As I have recalled on several occasions, according to the Rule 1881 of the detention rules where a detainee is not satisfied with the condition of his and her detention, he or she is entitled to make a complaint to the commanding officer or his representative at any time. And in case of an unsatisfactory response to make a written complaint, without censorship, to the Registrar who shall inform the president. I myself also take into account your submissions today. We'll see what we could do in this aspect. Are there any other persons who would like to make some submissions? It seems to me none. Before we turn to any issue that parties may wish to raise, I would like to briefly mentioned one outstanding matter. On 15th of February, 2010, Mr. Lazarevic confidentially filed his reply brief in this case. As far as I'm aware, no public redacted version of his -- of this document has been filed. Accordingly, in my capacity as Presiding Judge, I hereby instruct Mr. Lazarevic to file a public redacted version of his reply brief no later than 15 October, 2013. Regarding any confidential information requiring redaction, I authorise Mr. Lazarevic consult the relevant decisions rendered in the present case including the decision under Prosecution's motion concerning confidential information on Lazarevic's public submission, dated 31st March, 2010, and the decision under Prosecution's Second Motion regarding confidential information in Lazarevic's public submission dated 1st of June, 2010. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise. Is there any issue that Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no issues to raise, Your Honour. I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I turn to counsel for Mr. Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Nothing. We have nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The counsel for Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Counsel for Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have nothing and my apologies for the omission that our Defence made with respect to the redacted version of the reply brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance and adjourn these proceedings.
